utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Registrar, good afternoon to you. Could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-03-68-T, the Prosecutor versus Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you so much. Mr. Oric, can you follow the proceedings in your own language?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours, ladies and gentlemen. Yes, I can follow the proceedings in my own language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. You may sit down, and good afternoon to you. Mr. Wubben, good afternoon to you. Appearances for the Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours, as well presenting the Prosecution is Mr. Gramsci di Fazio and our case manager, Mrs. Donnica Henry-Frijlink. Also good afternoon to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Wubben, and good afternoon to you and your team. Appearances for Naser Oric?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon to my learned friends. My name is Vasvija Vidovic and together with Mr. John Jones, I appear for Mr. Oric. With us are our legal assistant, Ms. Jasmina Cosic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Ms. Vidovic and good afternoon to you and your team. Any preliminaries? Yes, Ms. Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, let me just confirm for the record that we do not intend to respond to the Miletic Defence submission for access to confidential material in our case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. In fact, that was the first thing I was going to raise myself obviously because yesterday, of course, I imposed a time limit on the Defence, the understanding in my mind was that you were to take it for granted that you had exactly the same time within which to respond, with less interest maybe than the Prosecution has. The decision is basically ready so I will have it signed on the first break and that will be it. Actually, Judge Eser is correcting me. We will only have one break today as we did yesterday. Thanks to the cooperation of the rest of the staff, without which we wouldn't be able to do this. The other thing is this, the latest in the series of Defence motions, namely that asking for authorisation to inspect part of your archives, the Banja Luka, I forgot the -- Mauzer archive. Yes, can you respond to it orally now, Mr. Wubben, please so that we proceed with the decision?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Please bear me a moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honours, we've got the material. We are going to hand it over. It's just a question of compiling it and getting it and that should render the issue dealt with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you wish to comment on this, Ms. Vidovic or --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is all right. But we would like to receive a decision from the Chamber concerning this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So let's do it this way. We'll give you until the end of business day today, that's 4.30, to file any negative response or any other response that may qualify what you have just stated. After that, you have how much time do you require to hand over the documentation?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Just give me a moment, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Because I'm asking -- I'm asking this because to me in my mind at least there is a difference between -- do you have the motion here?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I don't have the motion here myself either, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The motion is to issue an order allowing the Defence to inspect the Mauzer material.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The way you have put it is that you have agreed to hand over to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Copies --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- of the entire Mauzer material.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: They can have it all, everything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Provided that's the case, but in other words I want to make sure that you're not making a selection.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: No, no, no. That's precisely what they -- they can have it all. And the only other thing that's raised is that there are some comments about the background to this material. Of course, we don't if we -- now that we've addressed you orally we haven't gone into that. About us, about the Prosecution. I don't think that we really need to go into that unless Your Honours want to hear from us about that but I think that our providing that material settles the matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Now, it's clear of course. The position as I put it earlier on, Mr. Di Fazio, was precisely due to the fact that first I did not have an indication of whether you were volunteering to or agreeing to hand over all the material and secondly, in handing over this material, whether you had any reservations, any qualifications because I haven't seen this material, I don't know what we are talking about, and maybe there is amongst this material some documents or videos or whatever that you need to address the Trial Chamber on. So I'm giving you up to the end of the day. If that's enough, also until tomorrow. However I wish to know more or less how much time you require, shortest possible time to hand over these.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I've checked. I've made inquiries. I haven't personally checked. I made inquiries about whether or not there is any material in there that would give the Prosecution any concerns. There isn't, apparently.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: That's all I want to say about that. As far as the delivery of the material is concerned I'm told it can be done, effected, done by Monday afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's fine. But there will be a decision, in other words. I think it's better to have a decision taking into consideration what has been stated by Mr. Di Fazio and, of course, twisting a little bit the gist of your application, of your request, that the inspection will consist in the delivery of the entire material. That would satisfy the request for inspection. All right? And it will, of course, -- the understand is that when you say that you are delivering the entire Mauzer archive, that you're making that statement on your responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I've made inquiries and that's what I'm clearly given to understand that we are capable of doing and we'll do it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But please check to make sure but because you make a statement here depending on the information you are receiving from others.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: That's right. I'll check and re-check again. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So any further matters? No? So, Professor Bilic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon to you, Professor Bilic and welcome back.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just make yourself comfortable. We are going to proceed with your cross-examination and I'm going to insist with Mr. Wubben to finish today, but in doing so I must also insist with you that you keep your answers as brief as possible. Otherwise you're going to stay here and it will go on and on and on. So Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Professor Bilic.

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon to you too, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I will continue my questions as I stopped yesterday and we will refer to your report, page 20. You stated in your report, page 20, that there must have been documents in the maintaining records of official documents, you pointed out to archives, within a span of time in their archiving that would not be contentious. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Doesn't that opinion also apply to the other two groups of so-called non-contentious documents related to Naser Oric and Hamdija Fejzic?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because the previous samples were close in time. There was not a big time span in between, whereas in this case, there was a long time period that had elapsed in the meantime of about 20 years.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Related to the documents signed by Hamed Salihovic, did that statement, that pointing out to the archives, did that form a reason that you called in your report for organising to find all the non-contentious documents with non-contentious signatures as evidence?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Wubben, I don't understand you. This is a legal question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: This is not a legal question. It's a matter of organisation to find and check. There is in my opinion, Professor Bilic, I quote page 20, it's about, well, let me guess, the 15th line, "it should have been organised to find and present to the Tribunal of the Prosecutor or the Prosecutor, sorry, all the accompanying non-contentious documents with non-contentious signatures and handwriting by HS as evidence, et cetera." It should have been organised. Had it been organised, in fact?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of Hamed Salihovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If this is what you're referring to, this was not organised. This had to do with preparing a non-contentious sample of material.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you. A simple yes or no will do or, "I don't know" or "please clarify further your question."

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bilic. I will now move to the issue of methods of forensic examination. Professor Bilic, last Monday you stated that you critically re-test all the findings you have made after examination. You pointed out, and I quote, "That a person gets carried away over values or undervalues certain items and that in order to reach objective and high quality findings, one has to re-examine the findings. It is only at the end of this that conclusions are formed which are then structured along a scale of probability or possibility." Do you recall such a statement?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not the way I said it. I said that after the entire examination is over, when all the conclusions have been reached, what has been obtained is re-tested. This refers to both contentious and non-contentious documents. Only after this can actual conclusions be presented. That's my method of work, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. I consider that as a second similar opinion. My quotation was from a -- Monday, quarter after three in the afternoon. Now, in this context, are you familiar with the phenomenon of a shadow examiner when it comes to forensic analysis?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean by "shadow"? In who's shadow? What shadow? I don't understand you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Meaning that a second expert also do the examination and the findings and then only a unanimous decision will be valid on behalf of the report. Are you familiar with such a shadow examiner, second examiner?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Do you agree that in order to reach objective and high quality findings, it would be better to include such a second so-called shadow examiner in conclusions?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in shadow. This should be public. He should be known. Everybody should know who he is. And it's a good idea to have more than one expert. However, if no other experts are available, then, of course, the possibility of having someone else work as a shadow examiner is reduced, but I feel that this is scientifically justified. It is only the expression "shadow" that I couldn't accept because when you say someone is in the shadow it means he is unofficial or semi-official or secret. However, this can be ordered by the Court or the Defence. There can be a second, a third, even a fourth expert. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Professor Bilic, what I mentioned is indeed a kind of second opinion but then next to you in your laboratory. So independent from each other, you and that second examiner reach a conclusion and compare to each other and only the unanimous conclusion is valid. Do you agree that that is a better way to make analysis?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In some cases, yes, but not necessarily.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It all depends on whether the second expert is as able as the first expert. The expert should be on the same level. They should both have the same level of ability. And that is for a third party to evaluate. Only two experts with the same experience and background can be taken into consideration. That's my conclusion now although it need not be a definite one.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Do you mean that different experiences and background lead to different opinions and conclusions?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not like that. There might be some differences, but the conclusions would not be extremely different. Again, this has to do with the ability, knowledge, and experience of the investigator. I do not know what knowledge, experience, and abilities the other investigator has. We are not the same, either as human beings or as investigators.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Professor Bilic, I only spoke in this context in a theoretical way because you don't have a second examiner next to you, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could have had. There are quite a few. But my mandate was quite different. I was recruited as a single individual, as an expert. I didn't think I was allowed to show this to anyone or discuss it with anyone. This was confidential material. I couldn't bandy around and show to all and sundry, so those were my reservations. I have quite a few colleagues, assistants, good investigators in Banja Luka and Sarajevo, who do a good job. There were people I trained and many of them have already got their Ph.D.s, but I worked on my own, pursuant to my mandate. I work conscientiously but this is the reason why I did not work together with another investigator who would test and re-test my conclusions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Is it true that you considered a second examiner, second investigator, next to you?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't even consider it because it wasn't in my mandate.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: In your report, page 24, you refer to the rating scale. It's below in the page, around eight lines from [indiscernible]?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Isn't that clarified rating of your scale limited?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a very rough scale. This kind of scale varies from expert to expert. There can be more or less --

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Professor Bilic, just yes or no or you don't know. Why didn't you explain the whole applied scale, including the ones left?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't feel it to be necessary in this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Wouldn't a complete applied scale, so the ratings applied by you, mean a clarification, more a clarification, and make your report more transparent for the readers?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very finely tuned scales, breaking it all up into lots of little segments might be confusing, misleading. They would not give a clear answer. In view of the material I had at my disposal, I did not feel it necessary to say possibly, more probably, bordering on certainty, and so on and so forth. I didn't feel it was required in this particular case, and this is what I stated in my conclusions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you. I turn now to P46. That's document number S-1 related to Hamed Salihovic. In your report -- well, I might --

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I considered, Your Honour, to call the usher to bring it on the ELMO. Can we first try to do it without? Perhaps that will expedite?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Alternatively, Mr. Wubben, if you could perhaps through one of your -- the case manager indicate on a piece of paper to my staff, to our staff, the documents that you may be requiring to put on the ELMO so they have them prepared already. You just have to refer to them and they will be on the ELMO in five seconds. P46.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: We have the originals here ready to go, so that's even better.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's even easier.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Put it on the ELMO. Thank you very much, Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: So please show the seal, Madam Usher. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: In your report, Professor Bilic, you stated that a round seal -- you referred to a round seal covering the signature and that the seal did indeed limit and makes more difficult analysis of the contentious signature. Why did you state that in your report?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stated that because, first of all, you don't see it with the naked eye. You can however see it using instruments.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes. But what about the use of infrared and U.V. and stereo microscope? Doesn't that make that in fact easy? So a round seal covering does not limit and makes it more difficult or you mean it in the context I just take a look at it?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is for the readers of these findings. It's quite complicated to describe how you view this through infrared light, how you put filters on a microscope and so on. It would only make the report more complicated. But, of course, these instruments are used and it is not a problem to use them. However, I put in this statement for those who are simply looking at this without instruments and this is actually the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And if this document was a photocopy, was it also then more difficult to examine and to conclude?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It would be quite difficult, bordering on possibility. As you know, in principle, photocopies make it even more difficult. Therefore, you're right, Mr. Wubben, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Next exhibit, please, Madam Usher, D1014. That's S-2, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Wubben? Please go ahead with your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: In your report, Professor Bilic, you stated that on the first page, "It's clearly visible that there is a correction in the handwriting, using a red pencil, and further on, and at the same time written figures in a date, a blue ballpoint pen where the number 3 is a truly amateur correction into 2." My question is, what do you mean by "truly amateur correction"? What does it constitutes in your analysis?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This term or rather translation as amateur wasn't really adequate. I said ineptly. So if the person wanted to change the year 1993, then the writer should have used a blue ballpoint pen rather than a red crayon, which is actually used for colouring drawings. That's the elementary thing I wanted to say. I don't know how it should have been translated in English. I don't know English. But that's what I wanted to say, that -- you can see it from there how ineptly it was done and it was in that sense that I made that comment, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: But why should it be done in blue? Can't it just be a correction like any other correction?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But my question to you would be why was it done in red? And, of course, we could go on with questions like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: M'hm. But you were the first to state that it should be in blue, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could have been done in purple.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And would that make the document suspicious, constitutes any forgery?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't say that it was a forgery, but it does add to make the document suspect. We were talking about suspect documents and about the features, the specific features they have. I believe I gave you a clear answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Judge Eser? And then Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Just one small correction. There was a -- translated as crayon, what I think should have been pencil. It's just a very small matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's not a small matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Professor Bilic, I have a question. If you speak of inept, it was an inept correction, the question is inept in what regard? I mean, if it was to hide a forgery, then it was obviously inept, but if it was a pure correction that somebody realised that it was -- the year was wrong, it would be even good to have it in red, to make clear that it had been corrected. So inept is a little bit ambivalent characterisation. Inept in what respect?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I meant to say the following. If the writer wanted to correct the number, then he should have erased number 3 and placed number 2 instead. This would have been a proper way of doing it. In correspondence, this is something that is not proper. Even if it were an official document, then the correction should have been accompanied by a stamp. The case was probably the following. The person wrote number 3 and then at a second glance realised that he had made a mistake and then made this sort of correction. However, this is quite a striking, obvious correction. That's what I wanted to indicate. I don't know. Perhaps an adequate translation of the word in B/C/S, "nemuste," [phoen] inept, sounds strange in English, but that's the way I put it, and I adhere to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: So there is no suspicious element in that, that makes us think of forgery or suspicious alteration? Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I disagree.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: So you consider this as a suspicious alteration?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: May I ask the usher for Exhibit D1013.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Wubben -- Ms. Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I wish to enter a correction into the record. I heard the witness well when he said that the number 3 should be crossed and that the person doing it should even put his initials next to that. That's what the witness stated, and was not reflected in the transcript. It can be checked with the witness, if you so please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think I heard him say so much. So it's not a problem. We can proceed. At least I understood him to be saying so much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You nodded. You've understood.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Madam Usher, can you please show the date on top on the ELMO? Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Now, this is an official document, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Judging by all that we see, this is a official document. I did not have this document, nor did I examine it. I wasn't given the document by the Defence. That's all I can tell you about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: So this is an official document. The year 2000 and so is changed in 2000 so, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Is there a stamp with it, together with it?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is one at the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: No. You stated earlier, prior to this, a minute ago, that there should be a stamp added to such an alteration in an official document, and you stated further, later on, that there should be initials. Please look at me, Professor Bilic. The Defence is no need to contact for.

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm listening to you and looking at you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: No, you were not looking --

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am, I am looking at you. I don't need to be cautioned about it all the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Please concentrate on the question, give Mr. Wubben your answer so that we move forward.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I kindly ask you to repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: My question is: Do you see initials next to this alteration, as you suggested prior in your statement to the Court?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see any initials.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Does that modification, that alteration of the year, without initials, in official stamp, make this document suspicious or this alteration or change suspicious?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to my methods and principles I'm governed by, I would consider it suspicious, yes, because there are no initials and there is no stamp. That's a rule and a principle that this is governed by.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Let me move to P48.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is document S-4 and I have a question regarding the signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: In your report, you stated that this was a -- this is the contentious, short signature. My question to you is this really a short signature, shortened signature, Professor Bilic?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: What do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Compared to the other series of signatures, because one cannot read Hamed Salihovic. You can see that there are sequences which can be longer or shorter.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Can we take a look at page -- the map, the folder, on -- in your report, page 26?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: May you please put it on the ELMO? And is it possible also to place 27? It's just for the overview, only if it's possible, Professor Bilic. It's a matter of zooming, I think. Stop, stop, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Now, if you take a look at all these signatures, and you might even move the paper left and to the right, if you compare it with other signatures, is this really, is signature S-4, is this really a shortened signature compared to the others?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's one category of shortened signatures. There are several. For instance, look at S-8, S-12 A, S-9 A. It is in this context that we ought to examine it. S-9 A, S-12 A, S-8 A. If you compare S-4 with these, then it would fall into the category of a shortened signature, because it definitely -- it's not -- is not a full version.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I will move to Exhibit P101. There are handwritten short notes and numbers in the documents and you identify this as written by X1 and X2. Does that makes -- those handwritten short notes, does that makes the document a suspicious document in your opinion?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And does that constitute in your opinion beginning of forgery or suspect of forgery?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a suspicious document. We've already defined that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: But my question referred to those handwritten short notes. Do those notes by themselves, do they as such constitute a forgery?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Notes do not constitute forgeries.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's put too generally that way. They cannot be called forgeries, simply for being notes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And the notes do not by themselves does not -- do not qualify the document as a forgery, isn't it, the whole document?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You seem to be guiding me through a maze. Why don't you clearly state what you mean? I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: In another way, if someone --

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Wubben, I did not understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you for stating that. I will rephrase my question. If someone or two persons --

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: -- did different short notes like this on a document, and you later on see the document, notifying two writers, making short notes, does that makes the whole document suspicious in a way like a forgery, a forged document?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I simply said that the document was suspicious. There are other features that define a forgery because the document was typed, signed, and stamped and it should not have any additions made to it. Whatever is subsequently added gives rise to suspicious that something was altered. It has been disturbed in one way or another. It has been tampered with, and all the more so because this is a frequently recurring phenomenon on all these documents, and when documents were being tampered with in this way, this clearly shows that all the documents as such are suspect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think it's clear enough what he is saying. Maybe you're not exactly, both of you, on the same wavelength. But basically what is being said is the following: If I draw up a document which is typed for me, and then I sign it with my own hand, and then Judge Eser, after that I have signed it, writes something on it, and it is passed on to Judge Brydensholt, who doesn't know that the written notes superimposed on the memo have been written by Judge Eser, he has every right to believe that those were written by me. Because after all, we have a document which is signed by me. So basically, I am supposedly signing to everything that there is on the document. The question arises, if indeed it is established that the handwritten part of that document is not attributable to me, it's attributable to someone else, does that mean that there is a forgery? And the answer is, he's not telling you that the forgery automatically results from the fact that there are two handwritings on the same document. It may result from other considerations. But the fact that there are two different handwritings in a document and the handwriting which is different from the signature is not authenticated, it makes the document suspicious in his eyes. This is what he is saying. And it should -- I mean, under normal circumstances, it wouldn't raise much eyebrows because it happens most of the time but in an expert's eyes, of course, if he doesn't pay attention to -- and give due attention to something like that, I mean, I would be extremely worried. This is the situation. I mean, he never said that the document is forged in his opinion, because there is handwriting which he attributes to X1. He just stated that there are two handwritings on that -- on the document, one by an unidentified X1 and a signature which he doesn't agree belongs to Hamed Salihovic. And it's on the basis of -- he can tell us on the basis of what he reaches his conclusion as to whether there is a forgery in this case or not, but I don't think he has related the forgery or the alleged forgery or the suspected forgery to the fact that there is a handwriting on the document apart from the signature. That's how I have understood it. If I have not understood it -- if I have misunderstood it completely --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What is your position on this, Professor Bilic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The question that you've been asked by Mr. Wubben is this: Does the fact that there is a handwriting on the document in addition to the typed part and the signature mean that automatically, therefore, this is a suspect document, that it directs your attention to a suspect forgery? This is what was asked for you. I never understood you to say that it is so. I understood you to say that it is a suspect document. You will look at it with apprehension. That's how I understood you. But if I have not understood you well, please correct me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. That's correct, Your Honour. His Honour Judge Agius understood well what I was saying and I stand by what I said. It's a suspect document and now, of course, it has to be examined in a special way to see how this came about and why, and then it can be established whether indeed it is a forgery or not. For the time being, it is considered to be suspect.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Shall I continue, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Of course, Mr. Wubben. I tried to help by clarifying.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: In my opinion, the answer on my first question should be no. And that was a simple answer. Now it is an extensive answer and I appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Please, Madam Usher, could you put on the ELMO, P19?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The break will be at 4.00, Mr. Wubben, so you have an ample 30 minutes plus. 4.00, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you. May I see the signature, please, Madam Usher? Okay. A little bit upper. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Professor Bilic for this help. You stated in your report that this is the fourth version of the short signature. What do you mean by "version"?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that the signatory who is purported to be Hamed Salihovic wrote an inconsistent signature here. We have several versions of the signature, which is self-evident. This version here carries certain features that cannot be noticed in the other versions. You can have a look at the map and see the versions of the signature that can be found in the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Professor Bilic, can one person have different versions of signatures?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think he answered that question yesterday and you even referred him to an extract from the -- Ellen's book.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I think -- I thought that that was the natural variation between the same version, between the same signatures, as such, with the same design. But what I'm referring to is when there are versions like a shortened version and a longer versions, these kind of versions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, okay. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Professor Bilic, can a single person have different versions like that, shortened, widened, initials, of course, but again --

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A person can have one to two versions. If there are more versions than that, then these are no longer the person's signatures.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, these are no longer signatures.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The signatory normally writes his or her signature consistently, always in the same way. As I said earlier in my testimony, a person who has to sign hundreds of documents a day will tend to shorten his signature. However, in -- if a person signs documents, he will tend to have consistent signatures that will be more or less the same, in terms of their length. The fact that the signature varies in these documents again gives rise to suspicion because these documents date from quite a short time period. Such a frequent occurrence of varying signatures is not something that is normally seen. What of his signatures in official documents whereas one's signature is checked, like his bank accounts, his cards and so on and so forth. This complicates the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: In your report, you stated that there was a pseudo destruction. What do you mean by pseudo destruction, page 14?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Thank you. By this, and I have clearly explained it here, I think you can read it, I would like it to be read, then there follows a fluent fourth version. I will later give a brief explanation. I don't know how it was translated but I was very precise here. So, Your Honours, could this be done? We will not have time to go into the explanation. So perhaps it might be best if this were read out, with your permission.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: No. Out of abundance of expediting this testimony, I will drop this question and I will go to the report --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Page 30. Page 30 of your report. And this is a map in which you clarified a number of differences. Now, Professor Bilic, I will wait for --

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to the signatures of -- you mean these signatures here?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: The signature, yes, on page 30. Please put --

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. You're referring to Naser Oric's signatures on page 30, the map with the contentious signatures of Naser Oric?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes. Put it on the ELMO, please. Madam Usher will -- I don't need that exhibit any more. Only page 30. Now, can you please point out the differences observed by you between the signatures S-2 and N.6, source 2, alleged non-contentious signature? No, it's the same page, in the middle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: To, page 30, please, S-2, page 30 the second group, S-2 and N.6.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Simon 2, yes, and the -- right to it. That's S-2. And next to it is N.6.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Can you please point out the differences, the main differences, observed by arrow?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will ask everyone to look at the map, Your Honours, and I will indicate the arrows. The most evident difference is this ending here, which -- not the ending, rather, but this bulge in a fluent line here, which is constantly present in all the signature, but it's lacking in this signature. It's the Cyrillic letter č. I have marked it here and it's missing in this signature here. The next evident difference is that between this segment, the large capital O, and the next segment, the small Cyrillic r. There is no line linking these two. However, in this signature, they are linked. This was introduced by the writer and is an element that should -- the writer introduced of his own. If you look at all the signatures, you will see that this is the same in all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Professor Bilic, may I please stop you? I was only asking about S-2 and N.6 for the purpose of comparing, and I will ask the usher now to put on the ELMO sheet number 1. I have copies available for Defence and for the Chamber, Your Honour. The top you are familiar with. Again, the copy of S-2 and N.6. Now, what I would like to draw your attention to is the lower part, with the blue frameworks. Can it be included, the whole page, Madam Usher? Isn't it true that between N.6, that's on the top of the right, and K-1, that's the first blue framework graphic in the middle left, yes, that there are also differences, relevant differences?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This signature and this one up here?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes, Professor Bilic.

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. These two signatures are the same. You have marked this characteristic here, but look at the other characteristics which are the same. You cannot have every characteristic on every signature, because no two signatures are mathematically identical, as if they were stamped out by a machine. So there are natural variations which always exist and which are normal, but if you look at the entire complex of features which I marked, you will see -- you can see that this -- there is no bulge here, no little bulge here, but we have the other features. You can see just a hint of it, but look at the other elements, look at this angle here. I won't go into a very detailed analysis because it would require a lot of time, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt you. The question was do you notice the differences between N.6 and N.5 or, so to say, K-1?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There are differences but not relevant ones, not preponderant ones which --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's enough. Your next question, Mr. Wubben?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Do you notice the differences whether it comes to the position and distance of the long stroke going throughout the signature?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Do you notice the difference also in the framework of the -- the blue frameworks of the other signatures shown?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to this stroke here?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Running across?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: The positioning and distance.

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The differences are insignificant. However, the similarities are considerable. Look at this ending here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Professor Bilic, I can accept?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just tapered.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: That's not my question. I'm now asking you for the differences between those and that's my question, and please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, it's just Your Honour the witness has answered time and again there are differences but they are not significant. I don't know how many times he's going to have to answer that same question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: If that's the answer to my question, then it is not an answer to my question because the question was what are the differences.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He's being trying to be more specific basically because then it's up to us to decide whether they are significant or not. I mean, of course, we take his opinion as an expert that there are significant and non-significant ones but we have a right or at least the Prosecution has a right to know which are the differences. From the expert's eye, at least, which is definitely wider than ours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Before -- I hate to interrupt my colleague, next time I will object against any remark or comment by my learned friend when it is in the presence of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: But, Your Honour, I've never understood the rule to be that any objection has to be in the absence of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Come on, yes. Anything else, Mr. Jones?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, for this exercise to be useful I trust that this page will be exhibited and that we refer to each one, K-1, K-9 -- so we know what ear talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I would be taking that for granted but I would be very surprised if it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. And may I, Your Honour, just say I'm exercising a lot of restraint in not objecting and I think Mr. Wubben need not be so belligerent when I make a simple objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So, please, Mr. Jones, continue restraining yourself and, Mr. Wubben, please try to be less belligerent and let's move.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I thought this was an adversarial system, Your Honour, and there should be no guidance of the witness anyhow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I have every interest in seeing this witness go today because otherwise we don't have a courtroom tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes. So am I, Your Honour, but I'm not the only player in the field.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I know. I know you have always cooperated, Mr. Wubben and I trust you will also today.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: If you notice the differences on this sheet number 1, the differences between S-2 and N.6, cannot those differences also fall within the natural variations of signatures from the same originator?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But let me ask you something, Mr. Wubben. Signatures such as K-6, K-9, K-11 and K-34 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, K-16, not 6.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not have these as far as I can recall and I don't know where you got these from.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I asked a question about the appearance to you and whether or not you could follow the line of my question to indicate whether or not there are differences. Not more, no expert examination on the spot.

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There are differences within the limits of variation, but they are the same signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I will now move to page 32 of your report, pointing out differences between signatures --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This document, what are we going to do with it?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I would like to tender it, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And this will become Prosecution Exhibit P.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: P619. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Professor Bilic, I apologise. I will move to another issue and we'll not make use of page 32. Yes. Yesterday, you accepted that there are variations that usually occur from specimen to specimen as a normal writing variation. You accepted this as basic knowledge; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In handwriting, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And doesn't that also underline that you should anyhow try to obtain as much as possible a quantity of handwriting to fulfil the need for such variations?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we are dealing with signatures, then we have to collect signatures. Handwriting likewise. We have stated that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Madam Usher, will you please put P73 on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Professor Bilic, yesterday you stated that this -- that the mechanical scraping or abrasion was done with an adequate implement. What do you mean by that? Is this a kind of tampering?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Is it a possibility that the traditional rubber has been used?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not find any microscopic traces of a rubber. These traces can never vanish completely. Mr. Ellen explained this on -- I don't know what page. This was done with a sharp implement, either a pen knife or a razor blade or something that abrades the surface of the paper.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And I should see that as a further clarification to your report?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: The next exhibit, please, P4.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: P4 relates to S-4 and I quote from your report, that on the documents there is a physical chemical destruction evident by the traces closer to the earlier analysed document, ERN 02139581. That's document S-9A. Does that part of your observation mean that those documents had been together?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot answer that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Let's now move to the other exhibits referring to photocopies, P176, P210, P213, P3, and P330.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: This is one of the photocopies, isn't it? Page 17?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please? Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: You stated in your report, Professor Bilic, that photocopies without correspondent originals gave raise to suspicion and my question is, isn't that out of order within the framework of a comparison report?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think that question is completely obscure. I don't know how the witness can be expected to answer that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What do you actually mean to be asking the witness? Because I don't understand it. I think I know what you mean by I quite agree with Mr. Jones that it is not clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Professor Bilic, if you're requested to compare documents, to analyse and to give your findings, isn't it out of order to state in your report that photocopies without corresponding original give rise to suspicion?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: In the -- in your report, you mentioned, on page 18 -- you mentioned, and I quote, "Although in this expert analysis the original of the contentious documents are not presented, only their black and white photocopies, we did conduct following the order by the Prosecutor a preliminary but rather limited investigation into the typed material, handwriting, handwriting, and signatures." What do you mean by following the order by the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I stand to be corrected, of course, but at least the text that I have, and I hope this will not give rise to another motion for a fresh translation, is following the request by the Defence, I have here. Not by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I believe that was corrected in the corrected version. That error was spotted and it was corrected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It should read what?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's what I have. Because I don't think you gave any instructions to the -- to Professor Bilic to start with.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: That's why --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I would be very surprised to read that in -- I stand to be corrected because, please, Mr. Wubben, don't misunderstand me. I have the two versions, the first one and the corrected one, but this is -- and I don't know which I'm reading from, to be honest with you, but I think I'm reading from the corrected one because that's the first one I have before me. My secretary would put that before the others.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I quoted from the first version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And that means that I offer my apologies. Whenever you might indicate that that is again something, please trigger me for that and I appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: So I will withdraw the question, Professor Bilic.

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: My question is does the quality of these photocopies allow for strong conclusions either positive or negative after analysis by you?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And -- but you draw the conclusion that these signatures were most probably not signed by NO, Naser Oric, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And isn't that a strong conclusion?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... firm conclusion?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Wubben, it is not a strong conclusion. Whatever is most probably always leaves room for consideration.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you. In your report, you mentioned the relevant factors regarding photocopies, and if I might recall them, the alleged non-convenience for expertise of signatures, the modest results of the analysis not allowing for a certainty and validity of results, the few relevant characteristics not having been detected, and the rise to suspicion and the maximum reserve for acceptance by an investigator. That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not use the word "maximum" but I did say there to be certain reservations, and that the probability had to be stated, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And even on Monday you stated that photocopies are misleading and that to carry out any subtle measurements or analysis on photocopies is highly uncertain, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. That's why the word "probability" is used.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's 4.00. Shall we have a break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, please. I'm insisting because of the recorders basically because we could stay a few more minutes. But I think we better stop here for 30 minutes and we'll resume at 4.30. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Professor Bilic, will you please go to page 23, showing the map -- showing your map in your folder in your report. I have a question for you regarding the comparison of the handwriting alleged to be from Hamed Salihovic and my question relates to N.5. First question: Is it a fact that a student writes neatly?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You're certainly not referring to my student days, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: When it comes to official documents or official filling in of forms related to university, isn't it a fact, Professor Bilic, that someone writes neatly, especially a student?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, we must define what writing neatly means. Is it calligraphy or is it writing as clearly as one can? We cannot really go into the realm of aesthetics in this sphere of work.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: But writing to be read clearly, isn't that so, Professor Bilic?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Is the alleged originator at the time 19 years old or something like that?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And is he, the alleged writer, also being forced to write within a lined frame?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as you can see, evidently, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And isn't there also a big difference in time between this alleged non-contentious document number N.5 and the document S-12A?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was stated also earlier, that the time that elapsed was quite a long one, some 20 years. I believe we already indicated that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Does these factors that I ask questions about, doesn't these all limit the natural variety and characteristics with a view to these documents?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Wubben, could you please put a more specific question to me?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Comparing these two documents and knowing these limitations or, better to say, these factors, doesn't that limit the probabilities when you do your analysis on those documents?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was one of the factors I took into consideration in my examination, and I said most probably he was not the writer. I indicated the reasoning that you mentioned by placing that qualification.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Professor Bilic, page 36 of your report, you concluded, under 2 that Hamed Salihovic most probably did not sign. Is such a conclusion bordering to certainty or not?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I clearly said most probably not signed by Hamed Salihovic. Now, the certainty you've been mentioning, I don't know, I believe it is for the Court to decide on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Given the limitations of the quantity of samples available and the difference in time between the documents and the so-called -- the contentious documents and the so-called non-contentious documents, isn't that conclusion too strong, too firm?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I made such a conclusion in order for you, the Court and the Defence, to evaluate it. But it is my conclusion. The degree of certainty is something that I did not want to further weigh, and if you look at page 23 and the text contained therein, it will all become quite obvious to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Well, that's indeed for the Court to decide. I have a question related to page 26, 27, 28 of the report, Professor Bilic. In your report, you stated that regarding the cross analysis of the signatures, that all the signatures in the contentious documents were first mutually compared. The gradual comparison proved that there is a striking elementary difference. Now, can you please put it on the ELMO, Professor Bilic, page 26, 27, 28? Is that possible to do it in a kind of visual way?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Wubben, I did as much on this map. I placed these markings.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes. Professor Bilic, may I stop you --

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which bring us two into certain relation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I haven't put my question yet. Is it possible, Madam Usher, to show more of the contentious documents, I mean zooming out instead of in? Because Your Honours, I trust that you also can?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We can follow, Mr. Wubben. We've put them all spread out in front of us, but I don't think that Madam Usher can help you more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Professor Bilic, when you take the contentious signatures, the three columns of the contentious signatures, isn't it true that these signatures appear not to be striking elementary different? But there is a common shared model, a common shared design? Do you agree with that proposition?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't agree. This may only seem so to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes. But that's why I put to you my proposition, and you disagree. My question is what about the differences that appear -- Madam Usher might help me -- that appear in comparing N.10, N.10, and N.9? These are non-contentious. Are these two similar in appearance? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: With natural variety?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And please compare S-10 and N.11.

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These two.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Are these also in their appearance the same or do they show differences?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When you look at it with the naked eye, the differences are obvious. There are not even the most basic of similarities here. When you look at the entire construction of the signature from the first to the last stroke, you see that Salihovic is always written on the writing line whereas all the incriminated signatures are above the line. When you look at signature N.11, and the other signatures, wherever there is a line, they -- the signatures rest on the line, and these are some of the rules that a person who is accustomed to writing his own signature will never change. Look at S-10, S-11. If you take a look at it, I believe that it is clearly to be seen, and the -- as it is placed here, I believe it's quite obvious.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And between S-11 and N.13?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: S-11 is contentious, is a contentious signature, and as for N.13 and N.14, I indicated before that I considered these signatures suspect, of suspicious origin, I did not take them into consideration in my examination. I received these documents, I placed them on the list, but I did not include them in the comparison I made. If you take a look at the signatures, you will see why I did so. I merely placed them on the list out of consideration for the Defence who sent them to me, but I did not use them in my comparison. I did not place any markings there and I did not make any indication of the fact that I used them in my examination because I did not. I believe that it is enough to take a look at the signature with the naked eye to see what I mean. I hope I have answered your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And Professor Bilic, if you take a look at S-7 on page 27 and N.11 on page 28, do you agree with my proposition that there is not a striking elementary difference?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are so many differences that I believe they could be visible from space.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: So you don't agree with my proposition?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, from outer space.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I will move now to the following part of your report, page 30 to 33. These are --

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a map, Mr. Wubben. It's the map. Thank you, Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: It's okay. Page -- your report, page 29, you refer to the -- to the signatures, the contentious signatures and non-contentious signatures alleged to be placed by Naser Oric, and that you -- in your opinion, the signature revealed total discrepancy?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Now, I will show you a sheet and have some questions about that. Please show sheet number 4. Copy for the parties, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Professor Bilic, what do you mean with total discrepancy between the compared contentious and alleged non-contentious signatures?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are so obvious that that's why I used the expression. I indicated these differences exhaustively and I only marked them to a certain extent on these maps. But they are quite evident. Take a look at N.5, K-16, then 23, then look at S-2, S-4, S-7. I don't know if you can see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Can the usher please zoom out --

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are such great differences in the general appearance, in the construction of contentious and non-contentious signatures, in their size. If you look at the initial stroke of this ellipsoid and then look at the other ones, look at the end of the signature, ending in letter č, look at the line of writing, the angle of writing, then the -- this element of a full stop at the end, then the end of the signature, which is completely different, this particular one, from all the other non-contentious signatures. Then look at the fact that at no point in time do we have the connective link between o and r that start -- at the start, because if you look at the contentious signatures, they all have them. Then look at this last part of the loop of the letter č. I was trying to indicate them in great detail, although I did not mention every single particular element. I do not normally do so. I try to merely present the most obvious ones and I did so in the map, and these were decisive elements in my -- in making my final conclusions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Professor Bilic, if my --

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: If I put it to you that these overview of contentious and so-called non-contentious documents, that they do not include a total discrepancy, even if you limit the signatures, the overview of signatures only to the two blue-framed one, N.5 and N.12, together with the red-framework above, do you agree with me that the overall design and model is the same, that there is basically the same structure and model?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, definitely not.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you. I have another sheet for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Shall we give this an exhibit number, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This will become P620. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Please bear me a moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Professor Bilic, in your comparison of -- yes -- can the usher please help to zoom out? Professor Bilic, in your report, you stated as manifested differences in the signatures, as differences in the document comparison between contentious signatures and so-called non-contentious signatures, the length zone of the horizontal dash in Cyrillic letters h and h at the end, that's the c, the altitudinal displacement in relation to the central segment of the signature. Now, my question is to you do you indicate within this overview a difference between the signatures when it pertains to this length zone of the horizontal dash?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't understand the question. I don't know if the witness does. Is he being asked to indicate something on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, he is, as I understand it. Correct me if I'm wrong, Mr. Wubben. The witness is being referred to this sheet of paper with five specimen signatures in each case with a horizontal line across the signature. He is being referred to comment on Mr. Wubben's statement regarding the length of that horizontal line. If I have understood the question right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If I haven't understood you right please correct me.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, because I noticed the witness keeps indicating something on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The witness keeps moving his pointer up and down and ...

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, I was under the impression he was doing what he thought was expected of him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm not giving that much importance because he is all the time moving. Yes, Professor Bilic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Professor Bilic, do you notice differences, variations, when it comes to the length zone of the horizontal dash within the signatures called as N.12, N.11, N.7, K-12, K-29, on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These strokes are not of the same length and this comes within the natural variation because a writer even if he were forced to write always a stroke of the same length, it is impossible. He will not be able to produce the same line geometrically. And I believe that suffices as an explanation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: So when you define the length zone of the horizontal dash in your report as a manifested difference between the contentious and the non-contentious documents, then at the same time you indicate between these signatures that such a length zone pertains to a natural variation?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you. I will move to --

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Can this -- I want to tender this as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. This will become Prosecution Exhibit P621, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, to raise something but for the last question, it's unclear to me whether these signatures refer to the signatures on this document or whether Mr. Wubben was referring to the differences in the length zone of the horizontal dash in the contentious and non-contentious documents. The question and answer are obscure, I'm afraid.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I still in my mind -- I still have a suspicion whether the witness understood the question well because reading it in English, it is not exactly clear. But instead of making suggestions myself in order to find out what he understood at least with -- from Mr. Wubben's question, before he gave his answer, I will read out exactly what Mr. Wubben asked you. And then you explain to me what you understood by it. Question: "So when you define the length zone of the horizontal dash in your report as a manifested difference between the contentious and the non-contentious documents, then at the same time you indicate that between these signatures that such a length zone pertains to a natural variation?" Now, that's exactly what Mr. Wubben was asking. I want to know for sure what Professor Bilic understood by that question. What did Mr. Wubben, according to you, ask you? And you answered "yes." Yes to which question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my answer was yes. This is an element of natural variation of one and the same signature of one and the same person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I'm going to leave it at that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: This document, then, so that's clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm not going to put any further questions myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Otherwise, I can re-examine but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You can re-examine, of course, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Otherwise it's clear when he says this, he's referring to this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Stop. Yes, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I turn now to page 30 of your report, Professor Bilic. Professor Bilic, please take a look at signature N.5, and Cyrillic grapheme of the letter H stands for the B/C/S C, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That grapheme isn't present here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: It's page 30, N.5, yes. So the final, the last character of the signature, and there is a dash through the upper loop, isn't it? Now, if you take a look at that specific dash crossing the upper loop of the last character -- yes, that's correct, you're pointing out the last character, the loop. If you compare that character from N.5 with another signature within the range of N.5, N.6, N.7 until N.12, do you notice the differences between those signatures, between those known signatures?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I notice those differences that belong to natural variation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: So not being manifested differences in characteristics on comparing like the contentious signatures with the alleged non-contentious signatures?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: What do you mean by "yes"? That these can be indeed natural variations and not manifested differences?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are natural variations, which always exist in N.5, N.6, N.7 and N.8, N.9, N.10, N.1, N.11, N.3 and N.1, just as on the previous sheet that you showed me containing non-contentious documents. This signature, N.5, was written at the request of the Prosecution. There was a date above it. NO wrote the signature on that day, as he did with the other signatures. This is a series of signatures made on the same day by one and the same writer. This shows the natural variation that always exists with every person and every signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Professor Bilic. Now I --

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: -- have a question regarding comparison of contentious with non-contentious signatures related to Hamdija Fejzic. You found a multitude of relevant differences, and I refer to page 34. What do you mean by that? Is that significant with a view to the natural variations within the so-called non-contentious documents or not?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What specifically, Mr. Wubben, are you asking me?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I asked you when you indicate that you find, based upon the comparison, a multitude of relevant differences --

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: -- what do you refer to? Differences within the so-called non-contentious documents, natural variations?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I clearly and precisely explained those differences and listed them on page 34. If you read this list, and look at the map, you will see that I have indeed mentioned what these differences are.
